label: Half hundredths equivalence
adaptation_note: Two same-scale 5×10 panels form one 10×10 grid. This changes simultaneous presentation, not the 100-cell denominator or selection count. The half-equivalence sequence also includes its separate two-equal-part reference whole.
acceptance_requirement: Across both panels retain 100 equal cells and exactly 50 individually marked cells. Keep the denominator 100, shared alignment and an explicit continuation cue; test marker-to-border blank pins.

frames.title: One half selected
frames.teaching_key: Reference whole split into two equal parts, left half selected by a sparse regular pin texture. Texture pins are a selection cue, not counted fractional units. The next two frames form one hundred grid with fifty selected cells: one half equals fifty hundredths. This reference rectangle and the grid have different drawing scales.

frames.title: Hundred grid: rows 1–5
frames.teaching_key: This is panel 1 of two equal-scale halves of one hundred grid. Read ten columns across and five rows down. Row range 1–5; whole denominator remains 100. A centre pin marks a selected cell. Exactly 50 of the full 100 cells are selected; no extra cell is introduced at the join.

frames.title: Hundred grid: rows 6–10
frames.teaching_key: This is panel 2 of two equal-scale halves of one hundred grid. Read ten columns across and five rows down. Row range 6–10; whole denominator remains 100. A centre pin marks a selected cell. Exactly 50 of the full 100 cells are selected; no extra cell is introduced at the join.
